newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Punjab cotton loses gains, low mill buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian Punjab cotton loses gains, low mill buying.

text.p: Indian Punjab cotton prices on Monday lost previous gains while Gujarat varieties were firm, dealers said.
Punjab cotton attracted profit-taking by local stockists watching the progress of monsoon and sluggish mill buying.
In spot deals Punjab saw-ginned fell by 25 rupees at 1,825/1,850 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Bengal-deshi fell by 25 rupees at 1,025/1,070 rupees per maund.
In the Gujarat segment, long-staple Sankar-4 was firm amidst a shortage of ready stock while Kala-ginned suffered a fresh setback on higher supplies against increased offerings by stockists.

In spot deals Sankar-4 rose by 200/500 rupees to 19,500/20,200 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) for the superior variety while Kala-ginned fell by 300/400 rupees to 11,800/11,900 rupees per candy. Kalyan cotton was steady at 13,900/14,000 rupees per candy.
